source-review.json.scope: Independent continuum mechanical derivation and saved-only fixture source review; no numerical oracle or production execution.
source_findings: The spatial rod tangent retains loaded-force and loaded-moment geometric terms and the symmetric distributed Ccg mass block.
The lower fin branch keeps the original increasing +z material orientation while integration proceeds toward decreasing coordinate; free-tip and point-jump signs are consistent.
The rigid-offset junction tangent includes the preload term (theta_B cross d) cross F_c.
Free-node frozen dead wrenches subtract both retained element endpoint actions and the kept boom-fin joint action. The removed connectors enter dead loads, while the cut balance belongs to its clamp.
The shared fin-root dead wrench is stored once and is zeroed in both branch load arrays.
The cut gauge rotates saved physical poses and wrenches while preserving literal rest geometry and property tables.
Literal EA/GKc/GKn are rigid; axis offsets and couplings vanish; distributed fin Ccg remains active even though sectional rotary-inertia entries are zero.
The original saved point-load locations are preserved under interval subdivision, with no model fitting or load regeneration.
source-review.json.integration_note: initial_root_moments and initial_root_moments_flat are material components; the spatial-M ODE must transform them with each rootmaterialrotation or use initial_root_trace_details[*].spatial_gauge.
independent_oracle_requirements: Do not import production Section, residual, geometry or mass assembly into the continuum oracle.
Retain all fixed spatial dead wrenches, with zero live gravity and zero fluid added mass in both benchmark models.
Generalize the independent single-rod utilities to variable property tables, three branches and the exact rigid offset; record the independent interpolation convention.
Decode production response normalization into physical feet and spatial radians before comparing two upper-tip input responses at 0, 0.7, 1 and 1.3 Hz.
limitations: This is a source and mathematical review, not numerical validation of the fixture, oracle or production benchmark.
The frozen-load clamped substructure differs from the full free-flight aircraft and is not an original-ASWING parity claim.
ASWING spline endpoint conventions remain unknown; independent interpolation and mesh/integration error must be reported separately.

production-response-conventions.json.scope: Prepared production exact nodal input sign, fixed-frame loaded-base rotation chart, and physical reaction recovery. No execution.

findings.subject: Input sign
findings.conclusion: B=+R_input is correct because A=R_z, M=-R_zdot and harmonic_solve solves (i*omega*M-A)z=B. Exact dead nodal force and couple enter residual rows positively, with scales F and F*L. Gauge input vectors are T times the original body-axis unit vectors.

findings.subject: Nodal output rotation
findings.conclusion: DynamicSystem uses r=r0+L*z_translation and Q=exp(z_rotation)*Q0. Therefore z_rotation is the spatial infinitesimal angle in gauge axes at the loaded base. Rotate translation and rotation by Qcut to original body axes. No base-Q Jacobian, degrees conversion or W factor belongs in these displacement/rotation outputs.

findings.subject: Reaction recovery
findings.conclusion: Ground output is the support wrench acting on the cut node. Joint output acts on node a (boom) as [F,T+d cross F], and node b (fin) as [-F,-T]. Its tangent is [deltaF,deltaT+deltaD cross Fbase+d cross deltaF]; the runner retains both lever-arm terms.

continuum_comparison_conventions.joint_moment_on_boom: m_U(root)-m_L(root)+d cross (p_U(root)-p_L(root))+(theta_B(tip) cross d) cross F_c = m_B(tip)
continuum_comparison_conventions.assumptions: Base dead wrenches have zero perturbation, cut dead load is zero, and retained joint is the rigid boom-a/fin-b connector. Rotate all continuum and production quantities to identical axes before comparison.

limitations: Source review does not establish numerical benchmark accuracy or convergence.
The source functions inspected in ROOT were confirmed byte-identical to the pinned C16 source actually imported by the prepared runner.

oracle-source-review.json.scope: Independent source-only check of the prepared continuum oracle, its mathematical restriction and frozen execution plan. No numerical computation or imports of the oracle/production.
findings: Static tangent uses spatial rotation and the loaded C*[M] term; each root guess is read explicitly in spatial gauge components.
All three branch directions and fixed-wrench jumps match the original increasing material orientation. The fin-root wrench occurs once.
The nine-variable equilibrium Jacobian and harmonic junction include the rotating preloaded-offset term with the correct sign.
The 18-unknown boundary system consistently uses scales [20 ft, 1 rad, 1 lb, 20 lb ft] for each three-vector group. Tip force/couple RHS and junction translations/moments respect those scales.
Independent natural cubic interpolation splits repeated knots and integration splits all property knots. The literal fixture has ten variable tables with valid repeated-knot segments.
Quartile output points cover the original node mesh and its two successive interval subdivisions; all four spatial vector groups are rotated correctly by the output einsum.

After the reviewed correction, harmonic acceptance is computed in the original 18-row boundary system after undoing column scaling, using the declared row-scaled and Frobenius formulas; internal equilibrated residual remains separately reported.
The single-child supervisor verifies frozen inputs, enforces the 180-second cap and single-thread environment, retains logs, and terminates/reaps the child on interruption or timeout.
oracle-source-review.json.corrected_during_review: Initial draft used internal equilibrated residual and different normalization for harmonic acceptance. Parent changed this before execution and retained the original unexecuted plan.
oracle-source-review.json.metadata_caveat: base.npz node states are after point-dead-load jumps along each branch traversal. response files select the first containing interval, hence pre-jump base N/M at shared stations. Position/rotation and incremental harmonic states are continuous; internal base traces must be labeled before any load comparison.
